title: One-hot EX forwarding selects
motivation: The measured worst path starts at the MEM/WB destination register and runs through the forwarding unit, EX, and the ALU to a memory-side output. The current forwarding network encodes priority into a two-bit selector and then decodes it again in EX, adding selection logic to a path that already includes operand forwarding and address generation.

hypothesis.motivation: The measured worst path starts at the MEM/WB destination register and runs through the forwarding unit, EX, and the ALU to a memory-side output. hypothesis.hypothesis: Replace the encoded forwarding selectors with mutually exclusive one-hot enables for the register-file, EX/MEM, and MEM/WB sources, and select each EX operand with a gated-OR network. This removes the priority-encoding-to-mux-decode hop from the MEM/WB register-index path, which should shorten the critical path to the memory outputs while preserving EX/MEM priority and x0 behavior.

lesson: - 2026-09-28 hyp-20260928-001-r1s0 (regression, +2.97%): Replacing encoded forwarding selectors with per-source one-hot enables and 32-bit gated-OR operands regressed fitness, suggesting the operand-wide mask/OR logic outweighed the selector-decode savings in this core.

title: Iterative multi-cycle integer divider
motivation: The measured critical path runs from a forwarded operand through the EX ALU, whose combinational signed and unsigned divide and remainder operators create a deep path. An iterative divider trades a bounded number of cycles on M-extension divide instructions for a much shorter clock period on the entire workload.

hypothesis.motivation: The measured critical path runs from a forwarded operand through the EX ALU, whose combinational signed and unsigned divide and remainder operators create a deep path. An iterative divider trades a bounded number of cycles on M-extension divide instructions for a much shorter clock period on the entire workload.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Move DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU out of the combinational ALU into a 32-step iterative divider. Add an EX-stage start/busy/done handshake that holds the dividing instruction and fetch/decode state until its quotient or remainder is ready, then allows it to retire once with the existing RV32M corner-case behavior. Preserve the ALTOPS substitutions for formal builds. Removing the combinational divider cone should materially raise Fmax, while CoreMark's modest divide use should limit the IPC cost.

Start and await division in EX, hold the in-flight instruction until completion, and emit its result and retirement exactly once.

Wire divider wait control through the pipeline so fetch/decode stop behind a divide and older instructions still drain without duplicate writeback or retirement.

title: Static backward branch prediction
motivation: Taken branches currently resolve in EX and flush the younger fetch/decode work, costing two cycles even for predictable loop branches. CoreMark has repeated backward loop branches and direct jumps, so resolving their next fetch address at fetch time should remove many of those bubbles.

hypothesis.motivation: Taken branches currently resolve in EX and flush the younger fetch/decode work, costing two cycles even for predictable loop branches. CoreMark has repeated backward loop branches and direct jumps, so resolving their next fetch address at fetch time should remove many of those bubbles.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a static predictor that predicts backward conditional branches taken, forward conditional branches not taken, and direct JAL instructions taken. Carry each fetched instruction's predicted next PC through ID/EX and compare it with the actual next PC in EX; request redirect and flush only on a mismatch. This avoids prediction-table area and leaves the forwarding and ALU datapaths unchanged while reducing control-transfer penalty on common loops.

title: Share EX branch comparison logic
motivation: The current worst timing path feeds the EX branch decision back through fetch and hazard control into ID. The branch comparator selects among several signed and unsigned relational expressions, which can create duplicated wide comparison logic on this feedback path.

hypothesis.motivation: The current worst timing path feeds the EX branch decision back through fetch and hazard control into ID. The branch comparator selects among several signed and unsigned relational expressions, which can create duplicated wide comparison logic on this feedback path.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Rewrite EX branch comparison to compute equality once and one unsigned comparison of the low 31 operand bits. Derive signed less-than from the sign bits and that shared comparison, derive greater-or-equal results by inversion, and select the requested condition with branch_op. This should reduce comparator logic and shorten the branch-to-hazard feedback path without changing pipeline behavior.

changes.description: Share equality and low-31-bit magnitude comparisons across the six branch conditions, deriving signed and greater-or-equal variants from sign bits and inversion.

title: Register branch redirects at EX/MEM
motivation: The best implementation has already removed the combinational divider, and the reported remaining path crosses EX, fetch, hazard control, and ID. Branch compare and target logic currently drive redirect and flush controls in the same cycle, coupling operand resolution to pipeline control and ID register selection. Registering the resolved redirect at the EX/MEM boundary should cut that long control path.

hypothesis.motivation: The best implementation has already removed the combinational divider, and the reported remaining path crosses EX, fetch, hazard control, and ID. Branch compare and target logic currently drive redirect and flush controls in the same cycle, coupling operand resolution to pipeline control and ID register selection. Registering the resolved redirect at the EX/MEM boundary should cut that long control path.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Retiming branch and jump redirects so the registered EX/MEM instruction drives the fetch redirect one cycle later should shorten the current EX-to-fetch-to-hazard-to-ID timing path and improve Fmax. The added branch penalty is bounded to one extra killed sequential instruction: use the registered branch/jump target and taken state, flush the younger ID/EX instruction and suppress its EX/MEM effects when redirecting, while allowing the older control-transfer instruction to retire with correct RVFI pc_wdata and trap behavior.

changes.description: Drive redirect and target from the registered EX/MEM control-transfer state, capture the correct JALR target, and squash the younger EX/MEM instruction when a delayed redirect fires.

lesson: - 2026-09-28 hyp-20260928-002-r2s1 (improvement, +12.40%): Registering the resolved branch/jump target and taken state in EX/MEM shortens the EX-to-fetch-to-hazard-to-ID control path, but the redirect cycle must squash younger EX work and its side effects while preserving the older transfer's retirement metadata.

title: Learned branch target buffer
motivation: The prior static predictor improved loop IPC slightly but regressed overall fitness because it computed target immediates and an adder from imem_data on the fetch-to-PC path. CoreMark repeatedly executes the same loop branches and jumps, so a small learned target table can keep target generation out of that path while avoiding EX redirect bubbles after the first encounters.

hypothesis.motivation: The prior static predictor improved loop IPC slightly but regressed overall fitness because it computed target immediates and an adder from imem_data on the fetch-to-PC path. CoreMark repeatedly executes the same loop branches and jumps, so a small learned target table can keep target generation out of that path while avoiding EX redirect bubbles after the first encounters.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add an eight-entry direct-mapped branch target buffer indexed and tagged by the fetch PC, with a two-bit saturating direction counter for conditional branches. On a tagged hit, IF can select the stored target without decoding an immediate or adding to the current instruction; EX trains the entry with the resolved target and branch outcome. Carry the predicted next PC with each instruction and redirect/flush only when EX resolves a different next PC. This should capture repeated CoreMark loops and jumps while avoiding the instruction-to-PC timing penalty that hurt the static predictor.
